title: Online Control Barrier Function Construction for Safety-Critical Motion Control of Manipulators
authors: Xuda Ding; Han Wang; Yi Ren; Y. Zheng; Cailian Chen; Jianping He
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Man and Cybernetics Systems
contribution: An online-constructed control barrier function filter for a 7-DOF manipulator that keeps millimetre clearances in cluttered scenes at about 39 ms per step, against 270 ms for TrajOpt.

title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
authors: Shilong Wang; Guibin Zhang; Miao Yu; Guancheng Wan; Fanci Meng; Chongye Guo; Kun Wang; Yang Wang
venue: Proceedings of the conference - Association for Computational Linguistics. Meeting
contribution: G-Safeguard detects compromised agents in LLM multi-agent systems with a GNN over the utterance graph and prunes their outgoing edges between rounds, cutting attack success at up to 80 agents.

title: Safe Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning with Natural Language Constraints
authors: Ziyan Wang; Meng Fang; Tristan Tomilin; Fei Fang; Yali Du
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
contribution: SMALL learns a language-model cost predictor from free-form natural-language constraints and uses it in Lagrangian multi-agent RL, reaching near-oracle constraint cost on the LaMaSafe benchmarks without ground-truth cost signals.

title: Secure Control of Connected and Automated Vehicles Using Trust-Aware Robust Event-Triggered Control Barrier Functions
authors: H. M. Sabbir Ahmad; Ehsan Sabouni; Akua Dickson; Wei Xiao; Christos G. Cassandras; Wenchao Li
venue: Symposium on Vehicle Security and Privacy (VehicleSec)
contribution: Trust-aware robust event-triggered CBFs keep connected vehicles safe at an intersection under Sybil and bias-injection attacks, with 95-99.96% safe scenarios under false positives where a non-robust baseline collides.

title: Adversarial Resilience for Sampled-Data Systems Under High-Relative-Degree Safety Constraints
authors: James Usevitch; Dimitra Panagou
contribution: A sampled-data CBF safety filter for multi-agent systems that stays safe against worst-case adversarial agents under asynchronous sampling and high relative degree, with a robustness margin whose removal produces violations in simulation.

title: Safety Under Uncertainty: Tight Bounds with Risk-Aware Control Barrier Functions
authors: Mitchell Black; Georgios Fainekos; Bardh Hoxha; Danil V. Prokhorov; Dimitra Panagou
venue: Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings
contribution: Derives risk-aware control barrier functions whose predicted failure probability closely matches measured failure rates, where the earlier stochastic CBF bound is loose, shown on a robot and a highway merge.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning Using Black-Box Reachability Analysis
authors: Mahmoud Selim; Amr Alanwar; Shreyas Kousik; Grace Gao; Marco Pavone; Karl Henrik Johansson
contribution: A reachability-based safety layer that needs no robot model keeps a learning agent at zero collisions in four simulated tasks while raising reward, with per-step compute under the 100 ms control period.

title: REFINE: Reachability-Based Trajectory Design Using Robust Feedback Linearization and Zonotopes
authors: Jinsun Liu; Yifei Shao; Lucas Lymburner; Hansen Qin; Vishrut Kaushik; Lena Trang; Ruiyang Wang; Vladimir Ivanović; Hongtei Eric Tseng; Ram Vasudevan
contribution: A reachability-based trajectory planner that guarantees not-at-fault driving under a hard planning deadline, falling back to a pre-verified stop, with zero crashes in 1000 simulated highway scenarios and on a scale car.

title: Multiagent Systems With CBF-Based Controllers: Collision Avoidance and Liveness From Instability
authors: Mrdjan Janković; Mario Santillo; Yan Wang
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
contribution: Shows that decentralized CBF safety filters can gridlock or go infeasible, and that a predictor-corrector variant (PCCA) matches centralized filtering with zero gridlocks and near-zero barrier violation in 100 five-agent runs.

title: Multi-Step Model Predictive Safety Filters: Reducing Chattering by Increasing the Prediction Horizon
authors: Federico Pizarro Bejarano; Lukas Brunke; Angela P. Schoellig
venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
contribution: Extending a predictive safety filter's objective over several future steps cut chattering about 80% on a real quadrotor versus the one-step filter, at up to 60% extra solve time.

title: Neural Control Barrier Functions for Safe Navigation
authors: Marvin Harms; Mihir Kulkarni; Nikhil Khedekar; Martin Jacquet; Kostas Alexis
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
contribution: Learns a LiDAR-conditioned neural control barrier function and runs it as an onboard safety filter on a quadrotor, avoiding collision in 95-99.7% of simulated rollouts at 4.4 ms inference.

title: NavRL: Learning Safe Flight in Dynamic Environments
authors: Zhefan Xu; Xinming Han; Haoyu Shen; Hanyu Jin; Kenji Shimada
contribution: Adds a velocity-obstacle safety shield to an RL flight policy, cutting dynamic-obstacle collisions per run from 2.70 to 0.85 in simulation, with shield runtime of 16 ms on a Jetson Orin NX.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning for Legged Locomotion
authors: Tsung-Yen Yang; Tingnan Zhang; Linda Luu; Sehoon Ha; Jie Tan; Wenhao Yu
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
contribution: Switches a legged robot from a learning policy to a recovery policy using a model-based reachability check, reporting 48.6% fewer falls than baselines in simulation and under five falls in 115 real minutes.

title: Safety on the Fly: Constructing Robust Safety Filters via Policy Control Barrier Functions at Runtime
authors: Luzia Knoedler; Oswin So; Ji Yin; Mitchell Black; Zachary Serlin; Panagiotis Tsiotras; Javier Alonso–Mora; Chuchu Fan
contribution: A robust safety filter whose barrier function is computed on the fly from sampled disturbance rollouts, cutting AutoRally crash rate from 0.80 to 0.09 and running at 100 Hz on a quadcopter.

title: Constraint-Guided Online Data Selection for Scalable Data-Driven Safety Filters in Uncertain Robotic Systems
authors: Jason J. Choi; Fernando Castañeda; Wonsuhk Jung; Bike Zhang; Claire Jennifer Tomlin; Koushil Sreenath
contribution: An online data-selection rule that lets a Gaussian-process safety filter meet a 25 ms control deadline, cutting solve time from 60.4 ms to 11.8 ms on a cart-pole with no constraint violations.

title: Tight Collision Probability for UAV Motion Planning in Uncertain Environment
authors: Tianyu Liu; Fu Zhang; Fei Gao; Jia Pan
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
contribution: Computes a tight collision probability for a UAV among uncertain moving obstacles and uses it as a chance constraint in real-time MPC, raising simulated mission success to 96-99% over more conservative bounds.

title: Sequential Neural Barriers for Scalable Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance
authors: Hongzhan Yu; Chiaki Hirayama; Chenning Yu; Sylvia Herbert; Sicun Gao
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
contribution: Composable sequential neural barrier functions, one per dynamic obstacle, filter candidate actions at runtime and keep collision rates low at up to 100x the obstacle density seen in training.

title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Shielding under Partial Observability
authors: Steven Carr; Nils Jansen; Sebastian Junges; Ufuk Topcu
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
contribution: Shields computed on belief supports from only the transition graph of a POMDP block unsafe actions of deep RL agents, cutting safety violations from thousands to zero during and after learning.

title: Risk-Aware Robot Control in Dynamic Environments Using Belief Control Barrier Functions
authors: Shaohang Han; Matti Vahs; Jana Tůmová
venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
contribution: A belief-space control barrier function filter bounds tail risk of collision from obstacle belief samples, reducing collisions from 54-72 to 1-3 per 100 runs at about 1 kHz in simulation.

title: Safety Aware Task Planning via Large Language Models in Robotics
authors: Azal Ahmad Khan; Michael Andrev; Muhammad Ali Murtaza; Sergio Aguilera; Rui Zhang; Jie Ding; Seth Hutchinson; Ali Anwar
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
contribution: A safety-auditing LLM beside the task planner reduces judged safety violations in multi-robot LLM plans by about 47% (GPT-4o) and 77.5% (DeepSeek-r1) on 40 COHERENT tasks, with CBF enforcement demonstrated on two mobile manipulators.

title: Safe Hierarchical Navigation in Crowded Dynamic Uncertain Environments
authors: Hongyi Chen; Shiyu Feng; Ye Zhao; Changliu Liu; Patricio Antonio Vela
venue: IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
contribution: Adding a per-step safe-set control filter beneath a gap-based planner cut simulated collisions among 20 and 50 moving agents from 8% and 29% to 0% and 3%.

title: Distributed Risk-Sensitive Safety Filters for Uncertain Discrete-Time Systems
authors: Armin Lederer; Erfaun Noorani; Andreas Krause
contribution: Lets each agent run its own risk-sensitive safety filter over shared global state without a negotiation round, closely matching a centralised filter on constraint violations for up to four simulated agents.

title: Safety Evaluation of Motion Plans Using Trajectory Predictors as Forward Reachable Set Estimators
authors: Kaustav Chakraborty; Zeyuan Feng; Sushant Veer; Apoorva Sharma; Wenhao Ding; Sever Topan; Boris Ivanovic; Marco Pavone; Somil Bansal
contribution: Conformally calibrated GMM predictors used as forward reachable sets give a plan-safety monitor with 5.83% balanced error in-distribution and 6.77-9.09% out-of-distribution, well below worst-case and prior calibrated baselines.

title: SICNav-Diffusion: Safe and Interactive Crowd Navigation With Diffusion Trajectory Predictions
authors: Sepehr Samavi; Anthony Lem; Fumiaki Sato; S P Chen; Qiao Lun Gu; Keijiro Yano; Angela P. Schoellig; Florian Shkurti
contribution: Joint diffusion trajectory prediction for all pedestrians coupled to a bilevel safe MPC, improving scene-level forecast error and reaching 1.00 simulated success with a 10 Hz real-robot loop.

title: SafeCast: Risk-responsive motion forecasting for autonomous vehicles
authors: Haicheng Liao; Hanlin Kong; Zhenning Li; Chengzhong Xu
contribution: SafeCast feeds Responsibility-Sensitive-Safety distances into a graph-attention forecaster of surrounding vehicles, reaching 1.54 m average RMSE on NGSIM with 235K parameters; it predicts motion and does not intercept actions.

title: Reachability-Based Confidence-Aware Probabilistic Collision Detection in Highway Driving
authors: Xinwei Wang; Zirui Li; Javier Alonso–Mora; Meng Wang
contribution: A reachability-based detector that computes confidence-aware collision probabilities for a neighbouring highway vehicle, flagging simulated cut-in crashes earlier than a heuristic Markov baseline at 30-50 ms per update.

title: Distributionally Robust CVaR-Based Safety Filtering for Motion Planning in Uncertain Environments
authors: Sleiman Safaoui; Tyler Holt Summers
venue: Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings
contribution: A distributionally robust CVaR safety filter that corrects a planner's reference trajectory against uncertain moving obstacles, avoiding the collisions seen with mean and plain-CVaR halfspaces in Monte Carlo simulation.

title: Optimal Control of Connected Automated Vehicles with Event-Triggered Control Barrier Functions: a Test Bed for Safe Optimal Merging
authors: Ehsan Sabouni; H. M. Sabbir Ahmad; Wei Xiao; Christos G. Cassandras; Wenchao Li
venue: IEEE Conference on Control Technology and Applications (CCTA)
contribution: Event-triggered CBF safety filtering for merging connected vehicles cuts infeasible QPs by up to 86% and QP solves by half or more versus time-driven control, validated on a multi-robot test bed.

title: DREAM: Decentralized Real-Time Asynchronous Probabilistic Trajectory Planning for Collision-Free Multirobot Navigation in Cluttered Environments
authors: Baskın Şenbaşlar; Gaurav S. Sukhatme
contribution: A decentralized probabilistic trajectory planner that keeps teammates collision-free under message delays and drops, reaching up to 2.15x the success rate of the best baseline with 16-32 robots among dynamic obstacles.

title: RVC-NMPC: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control With Reciprocal Velocity Constraints for Mutual Collision Avoidance in Agile UAV Flight
authors: Vít Krátký; Robert Pěnička; Parakh M. Gupta; Ondřej Procházka; Martin Saska
contribution: Decentralized NMPC with time-gated reciprocal velocity constraints gives collision-free agile flight for 10 UAVs at up to 25.9 m/s, running at 100 Hz onboard and tolerating 50 ms neighbour-state delay.

title: Voluntary Collusion with Secret Tools in Competing LLM Agents
authors: Xijie Zeng; Frank Rudzicz
contribution: Shows most tested LLM agents voluntarily adopt secret collusion tools (>=98% for 10 of 12 models), and that collusion cuts reward equality in Cleanup from 0.937 to 0.670 against a no-tool baseline.

title: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents
authors: Ziyan Wang; Shuqing Shi; James Oldfield; Samuele Marro; Jialin Yu; Philip Torr; Yali Du; Adel Bibi
contribution: BazaarBench measures delegation-safety failures of LLM agents in 100-agent simulated C2C marketplaces, showing that deadline pressure and adversarial instructions raise unsafe listings and linked completions for every tested model.

title: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Cooperative Tactical Deconfliction of Small Unmanned Aerial Systems
authors: Iman Sharifi; Alex Zongo; Peng Wei
contribution: Supervised LoRA fine-tuning of a 7B LLM as a per-aircraft speed-advisory policy cuts near mid-air collisions among 20-30 small UAS in BlueSky simulation relative to the pretrained model.

title: Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Small UAS Separation Assurance under GPS Degradation and Spoofing
authors: Alex Zongo; Filippos Fotiadis; Ufuk Topcu; Peng Wei
contribution: Adversarially trained multi-agent RL keeps small-UAS near-mid-air collisions near zero up to about 35% GPS observation corruption, versus about 25% for a nominally trained policy, in BlueSky simulation.

title: ForceFormer: Exploring Social Force and Transformer for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
authors: Weicheng Zhang; Hao Cheng; Fatema T. Johora; Monika Sester
contribution: ForceFormer feeds social-force features into a CVAE Transformer for multi-pedestrian trajectory prediction, cutting average FDE from 0.39 to 0.29 m and predicted collisions by about 20% versus AgentFormer on ETH/UCY.

title: Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Mason Nakamura; Abhinav Kumar; Saswat Das; Sahar Abdelnabi; Saaduddin Mahmud; Ferdinando Fioretto; Shlomo Zilberstein; Eugene Bagdasarian
contribution: An offline auditing framework that quantifies collusion among cooperating LLM agents through regret and coalition advantage, finding 57.89% of 19 models gain coalition advantage when given a secret channel without prompting.

title: MAMPS: Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Model Predictive Shielding
authors: Wenbo Zhang; Osbert Bastani; Vijay Kumar
contribution: A multi-agent model predictive shield that overrides MADDPG per agent with a verified backup policy, keeping all episodes collision-free while reaching goals far more often than a whole-system shield.

title: Refuse the Harm, Complete the Task via Graph-of-Rules Planning for LLM-Enabled Robots
authors: Ali Taheri; Alireza Taban; Qizhou Wang; Wanhua Li
contribution: A graph-of-rules pre-execution gate for LLM robot planners that refuses only the unsafe parts of an instruction, reporting 0% attack success and 84.54% task success on compound instructions.

title: XP-MARL: Auxiliary Prioritization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning to Address Non-Stationarity
authors: Jianye Xu; Omar Sobhy; Bassam Alrifaee
contribution: Learned priority ordering with action propagation among connected vehicles cuts the collision rate of a MAPPO baseline (1.09%) by 84.4% for a 2.2% loss in average speed.

title: A Hierarchical Variable Autonomy Mixed-Initiative Framework for Human-Robot Teaming in Mobile Robotics
authors: Dimitris Panagopoulos; Giannis Petousakis; Aniketh Ramesh; Tianshu Ruan; Grigoris Nikolaou; Rustam Stolkin; Manolis Chiou
contribution: A hierarchical mixed-initiative controller that uses operator attention and intent to decide when to switch control, reducing collisions, human-robot conflicts and unnecessary autonomy switches against EMICS in a 13-person study.
